summary: Defines MIB objects for managing ATM pseudowires, which carry ATM cells across packet switched networks.

eli5.summary: ATM sends data in tiny same-sized cells. This gives managers a dashboard for watching those cells travel through a modern packet network.

questions: what is the pw atm mib
how are atm cells carried over a packet network
subtitle: The SNMP objects used to configure and monitor ATM cell streams carried as pseudowires over a packet network.

tldr.problem: Operators who carry ATM cells across a packet switched network need a standard way to configure those emulated ATM connections and to measure how they perform.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 5605 defines the PW-ATM-MIB module. It adds a generic ATM configuration table, outbound and inbound tables (in 1:1 and N:1 forms) and performance tables for the current period, 15-minute intervals and one-day intervals.
tldr.outcome: A manager can map ATM interfaces and VPI/VCI values to pseudowires and watch cell and packet counters. It is a Proposed Standard and nothing in the metadata replaces it.

today: RFC 5605 is a Proposed Standard published in July 2009. The metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: What the MIB Manages
sections.content:
RFC 5605 describes a model for managing emulated ATM services over a Packet Switched Network (PSN). It follows the requirements for Pseudowire Emulation Edge-to-Edge and is closely related to the documents that define the ATM encapsulation and the ATM transparent cell transport service.

An ATM connection is a pseudowire (PW) connection. It is not treated as an interface and so is not represented in the ifTable. The module works with the ATM MIBs, the Interfaces MIB, the generic PW MIB (RFC 5601) and the textual conventions in RFC 5542.
sections.eli5: This document is the instruction panel for ATM lines that have been squeezed into packets so they can cross a computer network.

sections.title: Design Goals
sections.content:
The MIB module is designed to fit the PWE3 architecture and the generic PW MIB, and to fit the Virtual Path/Virtual Circuit (VP/VC) model of the ATM management MIB in RFC 2515. It also aims to:

  • Support manually configured and automatically configured ATM PWs.
  • Work with any type of PSN.
  • Support point-to-point connections. Point-to-multipoint and multipoint-to-point connections are left for future study.
  • Allow configuration of all parameters needed to establish a PW that carries ATM cells.
  • Report ATM performance metrics (cells transmitted, dropped and received, and unknown cells) as well as packet-level metrics.
  • Support ATM Operations, Administration, and Management (OAM) cells.

It does not consider Integrated Local Management Interface (ILMI) support.
sections.eli5: The authors wrote a list of jobs the dashboard must do, such as setting up lines and counting cells. They also wrote down which jobs they chose to leave for later.

sections.title: Relation to Other PW MIB Modules
sections.content:
A PW service is described by three layers of MIB modules working together, as set out in the PWE3 architecture of RFC 3985. The layering isolates PW services from the PSN layer that carries them.

  • The service layer holds service-specific modules such as this one. They glue the native ATM MIBs to the PW framework.
  • The generic PW layer is the PW-MIB module, which configures parameters common to all emulated services and PSNs.
  • The PSN layer has PSN-specific modules that tie the PW to one or more tunnels. For MPLS, the PW-MPLS MIB connects the PW to the MPLS-LDP or MPLS-TE MIBs.
sections.eli5: It is like three floors. The top floor knows about ATM, the middle floor knows about pseudowires in general, and the bottom floor knows about the particular network.

sections.title: Tables of the MIB Module
sections.content:
The module has four kinds of tables:

  • PW ATM Cfg table holds generic parameters that apply to every ATM PW.
  • PW ATM Outbound tables configure the PSN-bound direction. One table serves 1:1 service, and another serves N:1 service and transparent cell mode.
  • PW ATM Inbound tables configure the CE-bound direction in the same two forms.
  • PW ATM Perf tables come as a current table, a 15-minute interval table and a one-day interval table, aligned with the statistics of other PW services.

In the MIB objects, PSN-bound traffic is called outbound and CE-bound traffic is called inbound. The traffic parameter descriptor table is not part of this MIB, but each configuration table has an object that points to an entry in any ATM traffic descriptor table. A value of 0.0 means Best Effort.

The outbound table is filled for pwType values atmAal5SduVcc(2), atmCell1to1Vcc(12), atmCell1to1Vpc(13), atmAal5PduVcc(14) and atmTransparent(3). The N:1 tables hold up to N entries for atmCellNto1Vcc(9) or atmCellNto1Vpc(10), and also carry mapped VPI and VCI values generated at the egress. In transparent mode the VPI and VCI are shown as 0xFFFF.
sections.eli5: There is a table for the way in, a table for the way out, a table of shared settings and tables of scores. A pointer lets you attach a traffic rulebook from somewhere else.

sections.title: Configuration and Setup Example
sections.content:
The generic configuration table has four objects. pwAtmCfgMaxCellConcatenation (1 to 29) is the largest number of cells that may be concatenated into one PW packet toward the PSN, and a matching object records the far end's value. pwAtmCfgTimeoutMode says whether a packet may be sent when a timeout expires while collecting cells (notApplicable, disabled or enabled); the handling of the timeout is implementation-specific. pwAtmClpQosMapping says whether the Cell Loss Priority bits are used when setting the Quality-of-Service field of the encapsulation, such as the EXP bits of an MPLS label stack, so drop precedence is kept across the PSN. In transparent cell transport it MUST be false.

The RFC walks through an AAL5 PW. Cells enter through ATM interface 1000 with VPI 1 and VCI 100, and come back out the same way. The steps are to create a PW entry with pwType atmAal5SduVcc(2), then fill the configuration, outbound and inbound tables. The example sets the maximum cell concatenation to 29, turns the timeout mode on, turns CLP mapping off and supports OAM cells.
sections.eli5: You choose how many little cells to pack in each parcel and whether to send a half-full parcel when you get tired of waiting. The example shows one line set up from start to finish.

sections.title: Performance Counters
sections.content:
Each performance table adds ATM counters to the generic PW ones. They count missing packets, packets reordered, packets out of order, packets sent because a timeout expired, cells transmitted, cells dropped, cells received and unknown cells. Unknown cells are cells received from the PSN with an unknown VPI or VCI.

As in the other PW service MIBs, the current table covers the present 15-minute period. The interval table keeps earlier 15-minute periods, normally numbered 1 to 96 to cover a 24 hour period, and the one-day table keeps daily totals.
sections.eli5: The scoreboard counts cells sent, received and dropped, and it also counts strangers it did not recognize. It keeps one page for now, one for each quarter hour and one for each day.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Objects with read-write or read-create access can be dangerous in an unprotected environment. Unauthorized access to pwAtmOutboundTable, pwAtmInboundTable, pwAtmCfgTable, pwAtmOutboundNto1Table and pwAtmInboundNto1Table could disrupt network traffic. The configuration and performance tables also reveal ATM pseudowire topology and performance, so they may be sensitive.

The RFC says SNMPv3 VACM and USM MUST be used with any SNMPv3 agent that implements the module, recommends SNMPv3 cryptographic security, and says deploying SNMP versions before SNMPv3 is NOT RECOMMENDED.
sections.eli5: The dashboard could break the lines if the wrong person pressed its buttons, so only trusted people should get to use it.
